title: When mercy has to be received before it can be trusted
issueStatement: You are still reading the day through debt, performance, or self-punishment, so kindness feels suspicious instead of sustaining.
centralInsight: Gurbani places mercy near gift, nearness, and return. Grace is not a soft excuse; it is the condition that keeps return possible.
practicalReflection: Mercy changes the posture first. The heart stops negotiating for worthiness long enough to receive what the Guru is already giving.
actionPrompt: Before auditing yourself again, name one way grace has already met you today and answer from that place.

daily.label: Daily
daily.title: Mercy in the ordinary day
daily.issueStatement: By afternoon the day feels procedural, and mercy starts sounding like a word meant for larger crises or holier people.
daily.centralInsight: Gurbani does not wait for dramatic collapse before speaking of grace. Mercy belongs in errands, interruptions, and the plain shape of the day.
daily.practicalReflection: Ordinary time is where harshness usually becomes invisible. Receiving mercy there keeps the soul from hardening by habit.
daily.actionPrompt: Take one recurring part of the day and meet it with one line of gratitude before you meet it with critique.

pressure.label: Under Pressure
pressure.title: Mercy when the day tightens
pressure.issueStatement: When pressure rises, the first instinct is to drive harder, narrow the heart, and treat tenderness as a luxury you cannot afford.
pressure.centralInsight: Under pressure, mercy is not sentimental relief. It is the interruption that keeps urgency from becoming spiritual brutality.
pressure.practicalReflection: Pressure reveals what rules you. If the mind reaches first for force, Gurbani re-teaches it to reach for the Giver.
pressure.actionPrompt: Before solving the pressure, slow down enough to receive one line as shelter and let that line decide the next tone.

repair.label: After the Slip
repair.title: Mercy after the slip
repair.issueStatement: The mistake has already happened, and now shame wants to turn the aftermath into proof that return is no longer honest.
repair.centralInsight: Gurbani keeps mercy close to return. Repair begins when failure stops being theatre for the ego and becomes a doorway back to truth.
repair.practicalReflection: The mind often calls punishment sincerity. The Guru teaches a stricter honesty: admit the break, then come back without delay.
repair.actionPrompt: Name the slip without ornament, ask for mercy without bargaining, and make the next faithful act smaller than your shame wants.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: Learning a merciful way to live
practice.issueStatement: You can understand grace in flashes and still default to a punishing inner voice the rest of the week.
practice.centralInsight: Mercy becomes durable when it is practiced as posture, not only admired as doctrine. The Guru trains the heart to live received, not merely relieved.
practice.practicalReflection: A merciful life is not vague softness. It is disciplined refusal to build identity out of accusation and scarcity.
practice.actionPrompt: Choose one daily moment where you usually tighten against yourself and rehearse a truer, gentler response there for a week.
